newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Made in France? Shun it, Belgians told.
newsitem.headline: Made in France? Shun it, Belgians told.

text.p: Belgians should boycott products made by French companies in France to protest against the closure of carmaker Renault's Belgian plant, Belgian tabloid La Derniere Heure said on Tuesday.

Concerned about the 3,100 jobs which will be lost as a result of the shutdown of the assembly plant at Vilvoorde near Brussels, the paper called for an "intelligent boycott. Do not touch the products of French firms creating jobs (in Belgium)."

Outraged at Renault management's harsh decision to close a profitable and efficient plant in July, it said, "There is only one answer to the financial terrorism of Renault's state shareholder: boycott!"
The French state owns 46 percent of Renault.

A national cold-shouldering of Camembert cheese and Bordeaux wines was fine, but consumers should not blindly shun all French output since some 800 French companies represented in Belgium had created thousands of jobs.
The paper named financial services companies Axa and Paribas, brewer Alken-Maes and tyre group Michelin as examples of companies whose goods and services ought not to be boycotted.
France is Begium's third largest trading partner in the European Union with 1996 exports to Belgium worth an estimated 505 billion Belgian francs.
In Belgium, Renault is a top three make and sold just under 44,000 cars in 1996, after Volkswagen with about 78,500 units and Peugeot with some 57,000.
